title: Surgery in thm:atomic lacks framing/normal-map data needed to kill homology

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `thm:atomic`, Steps 1–3 (and inherited by `prop:induct`, `lem:simpconn`).

**The gap.** Rational homology of the null-bordism $V_0$ is killed by surgery on embedded spheres. The proof asserts the normal bundle of each surgered sphere is "stably trivial and hence trivial in this range." But $V_0$ is an **arbitrary** oriented null-bordism of $L$ with **no normal-map / bundle data attached**. For an embedded $S^i\hookrightarrow V_0$ representing a homology class, the normal bundle $\nu$ satisfies $TS^i\oplus\nu = TV_0|_{S^i}$, and there is in general **no reason** $\nu$ is stably trivial (that would require $TV_0|_{S^i}$ stably trivial). 

Surgery that **kills** a homology class requires a **trivialized** normal bundle (equivalently a framing / a normal-map structure); merely having an embedded representative (general position, $i<d/2$) is **not** sufficient. The standard mechanism guaranteeing framings is to surger a **degree-one normal map** $(f,b)\colon V_0\to (\text{target}, L)$ with bundle data $b$; that structure is never set up here.

**Affected sub-steps.**
- Step 2 (below middle): "framed embedded representative" is asserted without a source of framings.
- Step 3 (middle): the intersection-form / metabolic / signature-killing surgeries inherit the same deficiency (middle-dimensional surgery also needs the trivial-normal-bundle hypothesis $\lambda(x,x)=0$ **and** a framing).
- `lem:simpconn` equivariant $1$-surgery: same issue, $F$-equivariantly.

**Fix.** Reformulate Step 0 as a **degree-one normal map** to a $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic Poincaré pair (or frame against a fixed reference bundle), so all framings are supplied by the bundle map; then invoke the rational version of the surgery-below-the-middle / $\pi$–$\pi$ theorem. The rational target weakens the obstructions but the normal-map framework must be present, not skipped.
